title: Mrs. Kulwant Kaur vs Life Insurance Corporation Of India on 9 April, 2010
doc:
Mrs. Kulwant Kaur vs Life Insurance Corporation Of India on 9 April, 2010

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, PUNJAB,
         SCO NOS.3009-12, SECTOR 22-D, CHANDIGARH.

                         First Appeal No.324 of 2006

                                              Date of institution: 28.02.2006
                                              Date of decision : 09.04.2010

1.    Mrs. Kulwant Kaur widow of Nathu Singh alias Natha Singh;

2.    Sukhjant Singh son of Nathu Singh alias Natha Singh;

3.    Harcharan Singh son of Nathu Singh alias Natha Singh;

      All residents of House No.5/827 c/o Harkishan Singh, Old Suraj Nagri,
      Abohar.

4.    Paramjit Kaur aged 33 years daughter of Nathu Singh alias Natha Singh
      (wife of Gurbej Singh s/o Angrej Singh) r/o VPO Ramsara, Tehsil Abohar,
      District Ferozepur.

                                                                  .....Appellants
                          Versus

1.    Life Insurance Corporation of India, Divisional Office : Jeevan Udyog, City
      Centre Scheme, Post Box No.4, Amritsar-143001 through its Divisional
      Manager.

2.    Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India, Branch Abohar,
      District Ferozepur.

                                                                .....Respondents

                          First Appeal against the order dated 28.12.2005
                          passed by the District Consumer Disputes
                          Redressal Forum, Ferozepur.

Before:-

      Hon'ble Mr.Justice S.N.Aggarwal, President
              Mrs.Amarpreet Sharma, Member

Present:-

For the appellants : Sh.Gourave Bhayyia, Advocate For the respondents : Sh.B.J.Singh, Advocate JUSTICE S.N.AGGARWAL, PRESIDENT Nathu Singh husband of Kulwant Kaur appellant No.1 and father of Sukhjant Singh, Harcharan Singh and Paramjit Kaur appellants No.2 to 4 (in short "the appellants") had taken the life insurance policy from the appellants for an amount of Rs.4 lakhs with commencement date as 31.05.2001. He died on First Appeal No.324 of 2006 2 19.06.2001. The insurance claim was lodged with the respondents. It was repudiated. Alleging deficiency in service on the part of the respondents, the appellants filed a complaint against them in the learned District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Ferozepur (in short "the District Forum") for insurance claim. Compensation, interest and costs were also prayed.

2. The respondents filed the written reply. It was admitted that Nathu Singh alias Natha Singh had taken the life insurance policy from the respondents for an amount of Rs.4 lakhs while filling the proposal form on 31.05.2001. It was not denied that he had died on 19.06.2001 and the insurance claim lodged by the appellants was repudiated by the respondents.

3. It was further pleaded that Nathu Singh life assured was suffering from serious disease but he suppressed material facts with fraudulent intention while filling the proposal form. Therefore, the repudiation was legal and valid. Dismissal of the complaint was prayed.

4. Kulwant Kaur appellant filed her affidavit CA. Appellants No.2 to 4 filed their affidavits Ex.CB to Ex.CD. The appellant also proved documents Ex.C1 to Ex.C26. On the other hand, the respondents filed the affidavit of K.L.Khichi, Branch Manager dated 23.11.2005. The respondents also proved documents Ex.RA and Ex.RB.

5. After considering the pleadings of the parties and the affidavits/documents produced on the file by them, the learned District Forum dismissed the complaint vide impugned order dated 28.12.2005.

6. Hence, this appeal.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court reported as "Vidya v. Life Insurance Corporation of India and another, 2004 (3) RCR (Civil) 793" and it was prayed that the appeal be accepted and the impugned judgment dated 28.12.2005 be set aside and the appellants be awarded adequate compensation. First Appeal No.324 of 2006 3

8. On the other hand, the submission of the learned counsel for the respondents was that there was no merit in the present appeal and the same be dismissed.

9. Record has been perused. Submissions have been considered.

10. Admittedly, Nathu Singh had purchased the life insurance policy from the respondents by filling the proposal form on 31.05.2001. He had answered various parts of Question No.11 of the proposal form (Ex.C9) as under : - 

"Q.No.        Question                                            Answer Given

11(a)         During the last 5 years did you consult a               No
              Medical practitioner for any ailment
              Requiring treatment for more than a week?

11(b)         Have you ever been admitted to any hospital             No
              or Nursing Home for general check up
              observation treatment?

11(d)         Are you suffering from any disease pertaining           No

to liver, stomach, Heart, Lungs, Kidney, Brain or Nervous system?

11(e) Are you suffering or have you ever suffered from No Diabetes, Tuberculosis, High B/Pressure, Low B/P, Cancer, Epilepsy, Hernia or any other Disease?

11(i) What has been your usual state of health? Good"

11. The law has been settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a number of judgments that the contract of insurance is a contract of Uberrima fides and the parties are bound to disclose the material facts to each other. This law was settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment reported as "Mithoolal Nayak v. Life Insurance Corporation of India, AIR 1962 Supreme Court 814". It was held in this judgment that if the life insured suppressed the material facts with fraudulent intention then the insurer would be at liberty to repudiate the insurance claim.

12. The dictum of law has been reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the subsequent judgment reported as "Life Insurance Corpn. Of India & Ors. First Appeal No.324 of 2006 4 v. Asha Goel (Smt.) & Anr., I (2001) SLT 89 = (2001) 2 SCC 160" in which it was observed as under : -

"The contracts of insurance including the contract of life assurance are contracts uberimma fides and every fact of material (sic material fact) must be disclosed, otherwise, there is good ground for rescission of the contract. The duty to disclose material facts continues right up to the conclusion of the contract and also implies any material alteration in the character of the risk which may take place between the proposal and its acceptance. If there are any misstatements or suppression of material facts, the policy can be called into question. For determination of the question whether there has been suppression of any material facts it may be necessary to also examine whether the suppression relates to a fact which is in the exclusive knowledge of the person intending to take the policy and it could not be ascertained by reasonable enquiry by a prudent person."

13. This view of law has been approvably reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment reported as "P.C.Chacko & Anr v. Chairman, Life Insurance Corporation of India & Ors. III (2008) CPJ 78 (SC).

14. In order to prove that the information supplied by the life assured was false, the respondents have placed on the file, certificate of hospital treatment form No.3816 issued by Dr.Ravinder Sharma of Aditya Nursing Home Shri Ganganagar. As per this certificate, Nathu Singh was admitted in that hospital on 14.03.2000 and he was suffering from Chronic liver disease and Cirrhosis. He was discharged from the hospital on 17.03.2000 (Ex.RA). Cirrhosis has been defined in the Medical dictionary as under : -

First Appeal No.324 of 2006 5

"Cirrhosis : In it there is chronic damage to liver cells. It results in impaired function of liver. Heavy consumption of alcohol is the main cause of cirrhosis. Women are more susceptible to alcoholic cirrhosis. A special pattern of liver inflammation is present before cirrhosis. To start cirrhosis may be symptomless. Most common symptoms are mild jaundice, oedema, mental confusion and haematemesis. Men may loose body hair. Ascites develops due to low protein level in blood. High pressure in veins results in oesophageal varices. Coma and confusion result from accumulation of toxic material. Hepatoma, a primary cancer of liver may result as a complication. Diagnosis of cirrhosis is confirmed by biopsy."

15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court was pleased to observe in the judgment reported as "Satwant Kaur Sandhu v. New India Assurance Company Ltd." 2009 CTJ 956 (Supreme Court) (CP) as to what is a material fact. It was observed as under : -

"17. The terms "material fact" is not defined in the Act and, therefore, it has been understood and explained by the Courts in general terms to mean as any fact which would influence the judgment of a prudent insurer in fixing the premium or determining whether he would like to accept the risk. Any fact which goes to the root of the Contract of Insurance and has a bearing on the risk involved would be "material'.

16. It is, therefore, clearly proved that Natha Singh was suffering from a serious liver disease and Cirrhosis which was fatal in itself much prior to the filling of the proposal form but he suppressed these facts. First Appeal No.324 of 2006 6

17. So far as the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court in Vidya's case (supra) is concerned, it related only to mental depression or anxiety and it was held by the Hon'ble High Court that it did not amount to serious disease. Therefore, the facts of Vidya's case were entirely different. In the present case, the disease was very serious and the same has been suppressed by the life assured with fraudulent intention.

18. Moreover, the seriousness of the disease is clear from the fact that he died within 19 days after taking the insurance policy on 31.5.2001 as he died on 19.06.2001. The complaint has been rightly dismissed by the learned District Forum.

19. In view of the above discussions, there is no merit in the present appeal and the same is dismissed.

20. The arguments in this appeal were heard on 5.4.2010 and the order was reserved. Now the order be communicated to the parties.

21. The appeal could not be decided within the statutory period due to heavy pendency of Court cases.

(JUSTICE S.N.AGGARWAL) PRESIDENT (MRS.AMARPREET SHARMA) MEMBER April 09, 2010.

Paritosh
